thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: spike of 429s detected for tenant solstice.ai in vpc pool solstice-vpc-us-west-2. 5m window: 27% 429 rate, threshold 5%. auto-notify to oncall. links: https://monitoring.internal/alerts/2791234567

maya (oncall): Acknowledged. I'm paged and taking this. Can someone confirm if solstice pushed anything in the last 30m?

cust_solstice_ops: yes, we started a canary of a new model at 09:12 UTC (~30m ago). only 10% traffic to canary. seeing errors start ~09:30.

ash_sre: Thanks. Quick triage: checking pool saturation, rate limits, and KV cache pressure. Can you share a sample request id or curl from the failing cohort?

cust_solstice_ops: example request-id: req-0a1b2c3d; payload size ~ 3.2k tokens. I'll DM logs, but the pattern looks like repeated retry bursts from our inference client.

maya (oncall): Observed tail-latency increase and token-generation timeouts before 429s. Dedicated pool metrics: GPU util stable ~62% but queue length jumps aligned to spike. Might be internal throttling kicking in per-tenant.

ash_sre: Paging infra to check the tenant rate override table. runbook step 4: apply temporary per-tenant quota bump or route a small % to hosted fallback.

runbook-bot: Runbook command suggestion:
```\n# temporary per-tenant quota bump (admin API)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://admin.internal/tenants/solstice.ai/overrides \
  -d '{"type":"rate","delta_pct":50,"expires_in_sec":3600}'
```

lee (acct exec): FYI — solstice has an enterprise agreement. Any temporary increases need ops approval; we'll coordinate billing. They prefer quick relief over a prolonged outage.

carter (ops-lead): I'm online. We can approve a short emergency bump. Propose +40% for 45 minutes while customer rolls back the canary. Ops note: flag for contract reconciliation.

maya (oncall): Ash, do you want me to apply the admin override or do you want to run a diversion to hosted pool?

ash_sre: I'll apply the per-tenant override first — lower blast radius. If that doesn't normalize, we'll route 20% of solstice traffic to the hosted pool and enable KV prefix caching.

maya (oncall): Running the admin API now. Posting output.

maya (oncall): ```
POST /tenants/solstice.ai/overrides -> 200 OK
{"id":"ovr-7731","type":"rate","delta_pct":40,"expires_at":"2026-03-15T10:50:00Z"}
```

infra-deploy-bot: Detected config change: tenant-override ovr-7731 applied on pool solstice-vpc-us-west-2. Configsync OK.

maya (oncall): Monitoring... partial recovery visible — 429 rate down from 27% to 6% within 90s. Latency settling.

cust_solstice_ops: we are throttling their canary roll back to 0% now. thanks all.

lee (acct exec): Noted. Carter, please confirm billing flag and formal exception ticket. I'll inform the customer CSM that relief granted and will follow up on the post-incident invoice reconciliation. :thumbsup:

carter (ops-lead): Confirmed. Creating ticket OPS-INC-5942 to track emergency quota exception and billing.

ash_sre: Recommend follow-ups: 1) ask customer to remove the retry storm pattern and add jitter/backoff, 2) we should add a per-tenant spike detector to avoid automatic enforcement collisions, 3) schedule a short postmortem with solstice engineering and account team.

maya (oncall): All good from monitoring — baseline back to normal for 5 continuous minutes. I'm closing the pager but leaving the override to expire automatically. Will create incident doc and link OPS-INC-5942.

cust_solstice_ops: appreciate the quick help. we'll send a short RCA in 24h.

runbook-bot: Next steps appended to incident: create incident ticket, assign to ash_sre for RCA, run follow-up with customer in 24h.

maya (oncall): Summary: 09:30 UTC saw tenant 429 surge tied to canary + client retry pattern. Applied +40% temporary per-tenant quota (ovr-7731) at 09:33 UTC; 429s dropped to ~6% by 09:35 UTC; canary rolled back by customer; override set to expire at 10:50 UTC. OPS ticket OPS-INC-5942 created for billing/exception. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
